messages.author: 29907bb1ee07b7e3
messages.subject: DEC*
parts:
Hi Nick!

Hope everything is going great in Australia.

I saw your talk in the Evolution Meeting and was hoping to run BioGeoBEARS on my dataset including the models with the * "parameter" you and Katie Massana presented there. 
In your talk you mentioned that to implement the * model we should set include_null_range=FALSE.

I tried and got much better likelihood values under it so I want to confirm that I set it up correctly.

Here is what I did:

BioGeoBEARS_run_object = define_BioGeoBEARS_run()
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$force_sparse=FALSE
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$speedup=TRUE
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$use_optimx = TRUE
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$calc_ancprobs=TRUE 
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$max_range_size = max_range_size
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$include_null_range=FALSE
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$num_cores_to_use=2
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$force_sparse=FALSE
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$geogfn = geogfn
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$trfn = trfn
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object = readfiles_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$return_condlikes_table = TRUE
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$calc_TTL_loglike_from_condlikes_table = TRUE
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$calc_ancprobs = TRUE
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object
 BioGeoBEARS_run_object$BioGeoBEARS_model_object@params_table
 check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
 runslow = TRUE
 resfn = "CAFE_DEC*_M0_unconstrained_v1.Rdata"
if (runslow)
    {
    res = bears_optim_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object)
    res    

    save(res, file=resfn)
    resDEC = res
    } else {
    # Loads to "res"
    load(resfn)
    resDEC = res
    }

Does it look correct to you?

Thanks so much for your help, 
Vanessa Rivera.

messages.author: 0e713d20fc7459b5
messages.subject: Re: DEC*
parts:
Hi Vanessa,

did you saw Nick's co-authored paper in BioRxiv?

According to this manuscript it is indeed enough to change the highlighted line of code.

Also in my (strongly stratified) analysis DEC* clearly outperforms DEC and DEC+J. 
However, the manuscript mention the possibility that DEC*+J may incorporate the best of both of * and J and in my case it is indeed better by 6 AIC units.

Best wishes,
Torsten

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: DEC*
parts:
Hi -- yep, these results are the kinds of things I've seen as well.  What they *mean* can be more complex, we discuss this a fair bit in the discussion of the bioRxiv paper. One thing that is crucial is to *look* at the parameter estimates and *think* about what they mean for your specific case.  E.g. if e is superhigh that means instantaneous range contraction after any expansion event. This can happen because DEC* disallows the transition from 1 area to 0 areas, so there is no penalty for jacking e up very high to explain a dataset of single island endemics. This then becomes much like an anagenetic range-switching model.

But, other parameter combinations will mean other things..so, look and think!  And remember, reality will be much more complex than any 2 or 3 parameter model, so everything is about approximation...

Cheers,
Nick
